title: Armageddon as a kinetic war against the returning Son of God

tellings.quote: Armageddon is a war with the son of God returning to the earth. And I believe that's a kinetic war.
For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.
And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.
And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.
And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army.
And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.

plain: Armageddon, says a researcher named Tim Alberino, will be a real, physical war fought with weapons, which he calls a "kinetic war", waged by the powers of the earth against the Son of God when he returns. He tells Michels this as his own reading of the Bible, and he points to the Book of Revelation, the last book of the New Testament, written by a man named John on the island of Patmos and quoted here from the King James Version of 1611. In Revelation, unclean spirits "go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty", and they are gathered "into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon." Later John writes that he saw heaven opened and a rider on a white horse who "in righteousness he doth judge and make war", and "the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him." The rest are slain "with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth." The text does tell of armies gathered for a battle against the rider. Whether that battle is fought with real weapons, Alberino's kinetic war, is his reading of a sword that comes out of a mouth, and the text neither states it nor rules it out. If he is right, the end of days would be an actual armed conflict.

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: In the Revelation, Armageddon is the place where the kings of the earth are gathered "to the battle of that great day of God Almighty" (16:14, 16:16); the war against the rider on the white horse, whose "name is called The Word of God", is told in chapter 19, where the kings and their armies are "gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse", and the remnant are slain "with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth" (19:21). That this is a war fought with weapons, a kinetic war, is the teller's reading of a sword that comes out of the rider's mouth, which the text neither states nor excludes.
